prompt: We grow tomatoes in a glass greenhouse in the Netherlands. It's March and we're getting Botrytis in the plant heads and water droplets on the lower fruits in the morning. At night we run a 45 C minimum pipe temperature and keep our energy screen 95% closed with a 5% gap to get rid of humidity. Night RH is around 90%. What should we change?
assertions: Identifies heat emission / plant heads or fruits cooling below dew point as the cause of free water, not just high RH
Recommends closing the screen fully (no moisture gap) or a double screen, explaining that gaps drop cold air and create cold spots
Recommends removing moisture by condensation on the roof and/or ventilating above the closed screen instead of gapping
Recommends replacing or lowering the minimum pipe temperature and using fans (preferably vertical) for air movement
Addresses morning condensation on fruits: raise temperature gradually before sunrise and/or keep the screen closed until the air above it has warmed
Recommends monitoring absolute humidity / dew point versus crop temperature (e.g. aspirator box above the screen, leaf or fruit temperature)
